Simple algorythms. "New" means the newest post is at the top, no matter the topic or who posted it. "Hot" means the post with the most activity in the last (24? 12? 6? 1?) hours is at the top, regardless of topic, bias or opinion expressed.

Such a forum would expose the truth about the sway of the actual tide instead of what some "big brother" wants us to BELIEVE is the population's general consensus.

Remember when Facebook used to display to you everything your friends posted, right as they posted it? You know, kind of like Instragram does now? But now your friends can post things on Facebook every day, and, unless you visit their timeline directly, you may or may not see any of it, depending on whether the post meets Facebook's criteria of being worthy to show you. Now Reddit does the same thing, using algorithms to determine which topics are worth feeding the the front page or to r/all based on what they want you to believe about society.

Peer pressure is a huge factor in forming our opinions - if we believe that 89% of the population believes that socialism is the best way forward, someone with capitalist ideas will be more likely to keep it to themselves in order to avoid ridicule - except, of course, for a few zealots, who quickly become labeled, extremists. Likewise, the advocates of socialism become emboldened, believing that theirs is the popular majority view, and find the confidence to ridicule those who disagree. However, if it turns out that the promoted view is actually a minority, or even that the split is more like 35% socialists, 35% capitalists and 30% somewhere in between, then those from each view will be less likely to ridicule (expect for the *actual *extremists) and more likely to promote their ideas logically.

For another example, in the United States, the vast majority of people believe in God (92% as polled in 2011 http://www.gallup.com/poll/147887/Americans-Continue-Believe-God.aspx ), in at least some form, and that God was at least heavily involved in the creation of the universe and the life therein. Yet, if you look at the "front page of the internet", it will seem that at least 80% of the internet population believes otherwise, and, therefore, anyone who believes in God is a (insert degrading moniker).

If we had a less regulated system where popularity was portrayed and presented sincerely, the actual minority would feel like the minority, and the actual majority would gain confidence in their views. However, the 8% may feel that it's unfair that their view is not represented on the "front page", even though it's at the top of their favorite sub.
